items.content: The thunder came first as a low suggestion, then as a fact. From inside the house it was almost possible to believe that weather was something that happened to other people — to the garden, to the street, to the whole ordinary world — while inside remained permanent and warm and unchanged. She lit a second candle more for the smell than the light and watched the rain flatten the grass.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "watching a thunderstorm from inside a warm house". The polished structure and conceptually inventive metaphors are characteristic of language model output.

items.content: It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen.
items.explanation: Orwell's 1984 opens with this quietly unsettling detail. The juxtaposition of ordinary weather with 'clocks striking thirteen' signals wrongness — a distinctly human narrative technique.

items.content: The diner closed at eleven but he was still there at five to, nursing the last of his coffee, and she refilled it without asking because that was the rule for the last customer — you kept them as long as they needed, because the dark outside meant something and the light inside meant something else. He left a tip that was too large and she knew, without asking, that he had nowhere particular to go.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "the last customer in a closing diner". AI text often produces grammatically perfect sentences with slightly generic emotional beats — look for overly balanced structure and lack of truly surprising word choices.

items.content: The smell arrived before consciousness did: coffee, old wood, the particular mineral cold of a house that has been dark all night. She moved through it without turning on the lights, guided by the coffee, by the slight lessening of darkness in the east. There is a version of the world that exists only in this hour, she thought — orderly, unhurried, not yet belonging to the day.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "the smell of coffee in an empty kitchen at dawn". Notice the even pacing and absence of the kinds of small errors or tonal shifts that appear in prose written under genuine emotional pressure.
